subject: science
chapter_title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

concepts.title: The Human Eye - Structure and Working
concepts.definition: The human eye works like a camera: the cornea and crystalline lens focus light, the iris controls the pupil's size, the retina catches the image on light-sensitive cells, and the ciliary muscles change the lens thickness so the eye can focus near and far - its power of accommodation.
concepts.key_idea: Lens adjusts, retina records: accommodation keeps every distance in focus.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc110.txt section on the human eye structure and working

solution_steps.explain: Cornea, lens focus light through the pupil onto the retina.
Ciliary muscles change lens thickness for near and far objects.
Retinal cells convert the image to signals for the brain.

concepts.title: Defects of Vision and Their Correction
concepts.definition: Common vision defects are corrected with lenses: myopia, where distant objects blur because the image falls before the retina, needs a concave lens; hypermetropia, where near objects blur, needs a convex lens; and presbyopia in old age combines both, needing bifocals.
concepts.key_idea: Move the image back onto the retina: concave for myopia, convex for hypermetropia.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc110.txt sections on defects of vision and correction

solution_steps.explain: Check whether far objects or near objects blur.
Concave lens pulls a myopic image back; convex lens pushes a hypermetropic image forward.
The lens power in dioptres matches the defect's degree.

concepts.title: Dispersion, Scattering and the Colourful Sky
concepts.definition: White light splits into seven colours when it passes through a prism because each colour bends differently - dispersion; the same differential scattering makes the sky blue, sunsets red, and raindrops act as tiny prisms forming the rainbow, while near the horizon stars twinkle and planets do not.
concepts.key_idea: One white light, seven colours: dispersion and scattering paint the sky.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc110.txt sections on dispersion, scattering of light and atmospheric refraction
question_patterns: what is dispersion of light - explain with the prism experiment

why does the sun appear flattened at sunrise and sunset

solution_steps.explain: Prism separates white light into its seven colours.
Short blue wavelengths scatter most; long red wavelengths travel farthest.
Bending air layers twinkle stars and shift the sun's image.
